sourceContributions.qualification: New overlap mapping for the source's inflationary geometric-assumption and dynamics questions. Inherited assessments restrict it to generalized hyperinflation, distinguish side-tracked inflation and do not establish a classification of all rapid-turn models. Compatibility and reheating facets remain compound. Independent confirmation: u52 can specialize c0 through its geometric-assumption and inflationary-dynamics component. n31 and n84 restrict the assessment to generalized hyperinflation, distinguish side-tracked inflation and leave compatibility and reheating as separate compound facets.

The supplied setting does not itself furnish a calculated spectrum or correlation result, and shift symmetry is not imposed universally. Independent confirmation: u68 supplies a metric-dependent multifield setting relevant as a method contribution to c0. n60 specifically limits the target to geometric dependence of fluctuations, while n59 prevents imposing shift symmetry. The role claims no calculated spectrum.

Confirm the reused overview covers potential-free nonquadratic kinetic inflation in the Einstein frame. Decreasing curvature, acceptable perturbations and transition to radiation are linked source questions, not independently certified outcomes or potential-slope tests. Independent confirmation: Potential-free nonquadratic Einstein-frame kinetics is a concrete instance of c3's kinetic modifications. The contribution correctly preserves decreasing curvature, perturbations and radiation exit as linked questions rather than certified outcomes.

New mapping for the inflation, exit and perturbative-control components of scalar-coupled Gauss–Bonnet dynamics with the Einstein term retained and no assumed scalar slow roll. Adding a potential remains an intervention, not a universal premise. Independent confirmation: u31's inflationary component fits c3's scalar–gravity modifications and control target. Its retained Einstein term, absence of assumed scalar slow roll and optional added potential are explicit; its later-evolution component is not absorbed into this role.

Confirm the previously added mapping: the whole description explicitly asks about subsequent Einstein-dominated evolution. This is a later-evolution target within the unchanged compound source, not a verified successful history. Independent confirmation: Although c5 records earlier role disagreement, the supplied whole description directly asks about subsequent Einstein-dominated evolution, and n0 explicitly explains the added c5 mapping. This supports addresses without certifying a successful history.

The whole description explicitly asks how scalar–Gauss–Bonnet coupling modifies two-field rapid-turn inflation, potential slow-roll relations and consistency conditions. Only this early-time component receives the new role; its existing late-time roles remain unchanged. Independent confirmation: u70 directly addresses pq0's two-field rapid-turn dynamics, potential slow-roll relations and consistency conditions. The contribution is restricted to that early-time component and leaves existing late-time mappings and their matter conditions intact.
